raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in Manhattan, at Bethesda Terrace — the great stone gathering place at the middle of Central Park.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Take a moment. Let it land.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Now look up at the fountain — the winged figure crowning it is the Angel of the Waters.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"She's the work of Emma Stebbins, the first woman the city ever handed this kind of commission — and to this day, hers is the only sculpture in the entire park made by a woman.","source_id":"8d879d0a-f60c-4f2f-a234-e68bd0873932","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd"]},{"text":"How did a woman land that job in the 1860s? It didn't hurt that her brother was president of the Central Park Board of Commissioners.","source_id":"9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The angel blesses the water with one hand and carries a lily — the old symbol of purity — in the other.","source_id":"8d879d0a-f60c-4f2f-a234-e68bd0873932","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The fountain honors the Croton Aqueduct, which finally ended New York's water troubles in 1842; the structure itself was finished in 1864, and the angel dates to 1873.","source_id":"8d879d0a-f60c-4f2f-a234-e68bd0873932","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd"]},{"text":"So why \"Bethesda\"? The name comes from a pool in Jerusalem named in the Gospel of John, where the sick would wait for an angel to stir the water, then step in to be healed.","source_id":"9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"There's a debate about the angel that's never quite been settled — is it a man or a woman? Some read her as an early celebration of women; others point out that angels are sexless anyway, and Stebbins simply followed the design conventions of her time.","source_id":"9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Here's the odd part: this terrace was the one place in their whole design where Olmsted and Vaux wanted any statue at all, and they ended up with exactly one.","source_id":"9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The Moorish arcade you just walked under is the work of Jacob Wrey Mould, who had studied Islamic architecture and rebuilt its style right here; its ceiling once held thousands of tiles, and the Central Park Conservancy is putting them back now.","source_id":"9390b88f-f708-4a73-833e-49203ee3b3bd","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Off toward the water, the Loeb Boathouse has been renting out the rowboats bobbing on the lake since it joined the park in 1874, and it's a fine spot to eat.","source_id":"17409417-43e4-48c2-81da-edb359a6aed9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It even had its Hollywood moment — Carrie and Mr. Big of Sex and the City tumbled into the water off its dock at the end of a disastrous date.","source_id":"17409417-43e4-48c2-81da-edb359a6aed9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Walk north and you're on the Mall, the grand elm-lined walkway Olmsted and Vaux called the Promenade — their \"open air hall of reception,\" bedecked with statues.","source_id":"f1347821-815e-43a4-bf5a-e24e93634cc1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One of them, on your right, is Fitz-Greene Halleck, who died in 1867 and was once one of the most famous poets in the whole country — though almost nobody can name a line of his now.","source_id":"b41518e0-3632-4ac4-aa6d-8a1006306f0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Which makes the unveiling in 1876 almost unbelievable: President Rutherford B. Hayes came, his entire cabinet came, and ten thousand people crowded in for the ceremony.","source_id":"b41518e0-3632-4ac4-aa6d-8a1006306f0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That we've forgotten him says plenty about putting people on pedestals — a fashion well past its heyday.","source_id":"b41518e0-3632-4ac4-aa6d-8a1006306f0a","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"This same Mall saw a different kind of drama on June 22, 1901.","source_id":"268a9d59-aebc-4905-94e8-d96032e9f1e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The old benches had just been swapped for shiny green rocking chairs, and the instant you sat down, a uniformed attendant walked up demanding five cents for a chair with arms, three for one without.","source_id":"268a9d59-aebc-4905-94e8-d96032e9f1e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"An entrepreneur named Oscar Spate had wangled the rocking-chair franchise out of Tammany Hall, dreaming of two hundred and fifty dollars a day across the city's parks.","source_id":"268a9d59-aebc-4905-94e8-d96032e9f1e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"New Yorkers were having none of it. The angry public rioted, smashing and stealing the chairs.","source_id":"268a9d59-aebc-4905-94e8-d96032e9f1e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"A chastened Parks Commission yanked Spate's franchise and put out new chairs stamped \"For the Exclusive Use of Women and Children, FREE.\"","source_id":"268a9d59-aebc-4905-94e8-d96032e9f1e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"These days the Mall still throws a party — near its uptown end sits an underused band shell, and just west of it regulars dance-skate for hours every weekend to blasting disco.","source_id":"f1347821-815e-43a4-bf5a-e24e93634cc1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It's quite a scene.","source_id":"f1347821-815e-43a4-bf5a-e24e93634cc1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
